accounts_sentence: Active accounts are down 76% on a year ago, comparing 90-day averages.
bigquery_short: Run, and feeding the usage charts. Accounts match NearBlocks on 691 of 691 days, and transactions on 689
calls_sentence: Function calls are down 80% on a year ago, but the contracts being called have not gone away: about 1,194 on a typical day, against 1,165 a year ago.
cost_sentence: These 1,594 swaps do not spread smoothly. They bunch near 19, 77 and 146 bps. That looks like a price list, and no public document gives one. The documented public default is 20 bps. Stablecoin swaps cost a median 1.9 bps, close to the documented 1 bp. At the sampled rate, private swappers lose about $223.1K a day between entry and exit, against $60.2K a day reaching NEAR's wallets from every source. Part of that gap is solver spread and price movement. How much is fee, and who keeps it, cannot be seen.
explorer_short: Done. Run on 2026-11-08: 29% of DefiLlama's volume over 13 days, with 0 of 230,251 swaps labelled confidential. Its terms bar keeping the data, so only a summary is kept, and volume elsewhere comes from DefiLlama
explorer_test: We have not yet run it on the Explorer's own volume.
fee_by_size: 74 bps under $1K, 80 bps $1K to $10K, 119 bps over $10K
fit_sentence: A rough fit over 26 days puts a dollar crossing the boundary at about 2.8 bps to NEAR and any other dollar at about 5.5 bps. The 90% interval on the private figure runs from 0 to 14 bps, so it cannot settle the question yet.
flow_sentence: Money from accounts other than solvers went from 15% of reported volume before 27 October to 42% in the last seven days, about $52.2M a day. Accounts crossing each day went from 571 to 1,548. Counting solvers, the treasury turns over about every 1.7 days, so most of it is moving, not resting.
h_gap: For all three measures the 90% interval on the gap includes zero.
h_headline: Intents volume does not lead chain usage better than price does
h_sentence: Over 98 weeks, the last four weeks of volume told us little about the next four weeks of active accounts (rank correlation 0.18), and no more than price did (0.29). For transactions it was 0.04 against -0.09, and for function calls 0.01 against -0.08. For all three measures the 90% interval on the gap includes zero.
history_sentence: Monthly volume went from $6.4M in January 2025 to $4.0B in the last full month. Over the last 12 full months the trend is +46% a year, with large swings around it.
index_sentence: Over the last year, Intents volume rose about 3.7 times while active accounts fell 76%. The two are not moving together, so public chain activity no longer measures what NEAR is used for.
intents_sentence: intents.near took 1.0% of all NEAR transactions a year ago and 9.3% over the last 90 days. It went from the fifth busiest destination on the chain to the first.
path_sentence: For revenue to pay for all new NEAR by 2031, volume must grow +30% a year at today's take and the 1.6% floor, or +44% at the 2.5% cap. The recent trend is +46%. If private swaps pay NEAR nothing, the need rises to +69% a year. These cases are arithmetic on stated assumptions at today's NEAR price, not forecasts.
provenance_sentence: In the 60 days before 21 September, NEAR kept 2.83 bps of volume. Since then it has kept 5.06 bps. The part with no private trace barely moved, from 1.45 to 1.39 bps. All of the gain left the treasury first: 1.38 to 3.67 bps.
swaps_sentence: In 3 sampled hours before 27 October we saw about 18 private swaps an hour. In 7.7 hours since, about 519. These are only the swaps we can pair, so the true counts are higher.
txns_sentence: Transactions are down 84% on a year ago. Most of the fall came at the start of April 2026, when at most 3 signing accounts, sending 62% of all transactions, stopped.
